title: Feeling Sick: Making a Doctor's Appointment

vocabulary.note_en: not feeling well = a little sick

vocabulary.meaning_en: a common illness with a runny nose and cough
a body temperature higher than normal
stop working for a short time
a person who treats sick people

vocabulary.example: Stay warm and wear a sweater.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a fixed time to see someone
vocabulary.example: I want to make an appointment, please.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a loud sound when air comes out of your throat

fine_lines.title: I'm sick vs I have a cold
fine_lines.explanation_ar: مع المرض نستخدم be مع الصفة (I'm sick / I'm tired)، ونستخدم have مع اسم المرض (I have a cold / I have a fever / I have a cough).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use be + adjective (I'm sick, I'm tired) and have + illness (I have a cold, a fever, a cough).

expressions.meaning_en: Say you are a little sick.
expressions.example: I'm not feeling well. I have a headache.
I have a fever. That sounds awful.
You have a cold. You should rest at home.

expressions.phrase: Work can wait. Your health is more important!
expressions.meaning_ar: العمل يمكن أن ينتظر. صحتك أهم!
expressions.example: Go home. Work can wait. Your health is more important!

expressions.phrase: Have you seen a doctor? — No, I haven't.
expressions.meaning_en: Ask if someone saw a doctor.
expressions.example: Have you seen a doctor? Not yet.
Feel better soon. Take care of yourself.

expressions.phrase: I want to make an appointment, please.
expressions.meaning_ar: أريد أن أحجز موعدًا من فضلك.
expressions.meaning_en: Book a time at a clinic.
expressions.example: Hello. I want to make an appointment, please.

expressions.phrase: Why do you need to see the doctor?
expressions.example: Why do you need to see the doctor? I have a cough.

expressions.phrase: When would you like to come in?
expressions.example: When would you like to come in? Tomorrow morning.

expressions.phrase: How about 10:00 a.m.? Does that work for you?
expressions.meaning_ar: ما رأيك بالساعة العاشرة صباحًا؟ هل يناسبك ذلك؟
expressions.example: How about 3 p.m.? Does that work for you? Yes, that's good.

grammar.title: Talking about illness: have + illness
grammar.explanation_ar: نقول I have + a + اسم المرض: I have a cold. I have a fever. I have a cough. وفي السؤال: Do you have a fever? Yes, I do.
grammar.explanation_en: Use have + illness: I have a cold. Question: Do you have a fever?
examples: Do you have a fever? Yes, I do.

grammar.title: Advice: should / It's important to
grammar.explanation_ar: للنصيحة: You should + الفعل، أو It's important to + الفعل.
grammar.explanation_en: Advice: You should + verb / It's important to + verb.
examples: It's important to get a lot of sleep.

grammar.title: Making appointments: polite questions
grammar.explanation_ar: أسئلة مهذبة لحجز موعد: When would you like to come in? How about 10:00 a.m.? Does that work for you? Can I come tomorrow morning?
grammar.explanation_en: Polite questions for appointments: When would you like...? How about...? Does that work for you?
examples: When would you like to come in?
How about 10:00 a.m.? Does that work for you?

questions.question: A body temperature higher than normal is a ___.
questions.explanation_en: A fever is a high temperature.

questions.question: Have you seen a doctor? — No, I ___.
questions.explanation_ar: الجواب على Have you: No, I haven't.

questions.question: I want to make an ___, please.
When would you like to come ___?
How about 10:00 a.m.? Does that ___ for you?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد does الفعل في أصله: work.

questions.question: It's important ___ a lot of sleep.
